descriptionChirho: Physical running or swift movement on foot in all Qal finite forms, infinitives, imperatives, and cohortatives; Arabic rakada (رَكَضَ), Korean dallida (달리다), Swahili -kimbia.

Active participle used as a verbal adjective or generic substantive meaning 'one who runs, runner, running person'; Arabic raakid (رَاكِض) / addaa' (عَدَّاء), Korean dallineun ja (달리는 자), Swahili mkimbiaji.

Substantivized participle harratsim (הָרָצִים) denoting the king's bodyguard corps who served as executioners and sentries (1-2 Kings, 2 Chronicles); Arabic su'aat (سُعَاة), Korean chinwidaewon/gyeongbibyeong (친위대원/경비병), Swahili walinzi (guards).

Substantivized participle harratsim (הָרָצִים) denoting postal runners or royal couriers dispatched to deliver official messages (2 Chronicles 30, Esther 3:13-15); Arabic su'aat (سُعَاة), Korean baedalja/geupsa (배달자/급사), Swahili wajumbe (messengers).
Intensive stem conveying rapid darting or vigorous running motion; Arabic tarkudu (تَرْكُضُ), Korean dallidoda (달리도다), Swahili -nakimbia.

labelChirho: Hifil: cause to run, chase away
descriptionChirho: Causative stem meaning to make someone run, either driving them away in pursuit (chase) or rushing them to a destination (hurry someone along); Arabic asra'a (أَسْرَعَ) / arkadahu (أَرْكَضَهُ), Korean jjochanae-rira (쫓아내리라) / geuphi-deryeowatda (급히데려왔다), Swahili -kimbiza (cause to run).
